canvas-01.description: The northeast corner of Northfield against the Pleasantville city line, from Mapes Road and Maple Avenue at the top to Railroad Place and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line) along the bottom. Chestnut, Spruce, Walnut and Dolphin Avenues run up the sheet from New Road to Maple Avenue; below New Road the sheet shows Franklin Avenue and Second Avenue, both marked not opened, First Avenue, the short St. James Avenue, Dolphin Avenue continuing down the right side of the built area, and at the bottom Kendall Court and two proposed streets drawn dashed, all lettered arbitrary or proposed. Most blocks are large undivided tracts or deep lots with scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings, the densest group along New Road and around First Avenue and St. James Avenue. East of Dolphin Avenue, below the index panel, stand the buildings of the Atlantic County Tuberculosis Hospital: male and female wards joined by a kitchen and dining room, a laundry, an electric pump house and deep well, and a nurses' home. A 12-inch water pipe runs along New Road. The upper right of the sheet is given to the title cartouche, a key map of the town at 1200 feet to an inch and the street index; a water facilities and fire department report, a location map of New Jersey and the symbol key are printed in otherwise empty ground. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; sheet 2 adjoins on the left and sheet 3 below.
notes: Mapes Road and Maple Avenue are one line, now Maple Avenue; Franklin Avenue is now West Franklin Avenue; First Avenue is now 1st Street.
St. James Avenue does not match the modern St James Place, about 29 m away; it was not used as control.
Second Avenue and Franklin Avenue were not opened in 1924; their junction and Railroad Place (beside the track) were left out of the control.
Atlantic County Tuberculosis Hospital east of Dolphin Avenue.
Received stamp dated Jan 17 1925 beside the key map.

Sheet 1, 100 ft. Map with the title cartouche, 1200 ft key map and street index in a panel at upper right behind a heavy line (cut out of the mask), and a state location map, compass and key at lower right (key and compass notched). Mapes Rd/Maple Av (now Maple Avenue), Chestnut, Spruce, Walnut, Dolphin, New Rd, Franklin Av (now West Franklin Avenue), 2nd Av, 1st Av (now 1st Street), St. James Av (now St James Place), Kendall Ct, Railroad Pl, W.J.&S.R.R. Shore Fast Line. Atlantic County Tuberculosis Hospital. St. James Av does not match modern St James Place (about 29 m off) and was not used.

sheet-2.description: The western part of the grid of numbered blocks in the north of Northfield, between New Road and Mapes Road at the top and Fuae Avenue and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line, electric and steam) along the bottom. Five parallel avenues run up the sheet: Davis, Parker, Roosevelt, Jackson and Fairbanks, crossed by New Road, Second Avenue, First Avenue and Fuae Avenue; Tilton Road cuts diagonally across the upper left corner to meet New Road. Roosevelt Avenue north of New Road is marked not opened. The blocks are laid out in narrow house lots with arbitrary house numbers, most of them still vacant; the buildings are scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings with outbuildings, hen houses and a few garages, an auto repair shop on New Road and an automobile and storage building on Jackson Avenue. A block between Parker and Roosevelt Avenues south of First Avenue is marked as the site for a public school, and the upper left corner beyond Tilton Road is a farm. A 12-inch water pipe runs along New Road and a 6-inch pipe along Fairbanks Avenue. At the lower right the sheet takes in part of the block east of Fairbanks Avenue with the start of Kendall Court and Putting Green, and a small freight depot stands by the railroad at the foot of Roosevelt Avenue. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; sheet 1 adjoins on the right, sheet 5 on the left and sheet 4 below.
notes: Parker Avenue is now Mount Vernon Avenue (the name of its continuation south of the railroad).
Mapes Road is now Maple Avenue; First Avenue is now 1st Street.
The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line) along the bottom edge has since been removed.

100 ft. Grid between New Rd and Fuae Av: Davis, Parker (now Mount Vernon Avenue), Roosevelt, Jackson, Fairbanks Avs; 2nd Av, 1st Av (now 1st Street); Tilton Rd, Mapes Rd (now Maple Avenue); Putting Green, Kendall Ct. Site for public school.

sheet-3-1.description: The east end of Northfield along Shore Road up to the Pleasantville city limits, between the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line, electric and steam) and Railroad Place at the top and the Country Club of Atlantic City at the bottom. Putting Green, Haddon, Franklin, Virginia and Dolphin Avenues run down the sheet from the railroad to Shore Road and are crossed by Broad Street, drawn with a dashed line on each side marking a widened line of about 80 feet. Between Putting Green and Dolphin Avenue the blocks are cut into narrow house lots with scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings, densest along Franklin and Virginia Avenues near Shore Road; a small station stands on Railroad Place at Dolphin Avenue. East of Dolphin Avenue a large tract holds the Atlantic County Hospital for the Insane, a brick and frame quadrangle of male and female wards around a dining room and auditorium with a kitchen, boiler house, coal house, electric pump and artesian well, store and tool houses and elevated water tanks, and beyond it the Atlantic County Almshouse with its male and female wards, kitchen, dining hall and office, a barn with a silo and hog pens. South of Shore Road a lane leads into the country club grounds, with a few dwellings and a hen house. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch. A boxed inset of the Somers Brick Co works in the lower right corner is a separate part and is not included here.
notes: Franklin Avenue is now West Franklin Avenue.
Broad Street is drawn with dashed lines on both sides (a widened or proposed line of about 80 ft); today's Broad Street right-of-way is about 90 ft, so its junctions were used only where detected.
Atlantic County Hospital for the Insane and Atlantic County Almshouse east of Dolphin Avenue.
Shore Road / Franklin and Shore Road / Virginia carry residuals of about 4 m.

100 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main): Shore Rd between Putting Green and the Pleasantville line: Putting Green, Haddon, Franklin (now West Franklin Avenue), Virginia, Dolphin Avs, Broad (drawn with dashed widening lines), Railroad Pl; Atlantic County Hospital for the Insane and Almshouse; Country Club of Atlantic City. Part 2: boxed inset of the Somers Brick Co works at lower right (no streets, a railroad siding only); not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Somers Brick Co works (kilns, brick engine house, railroad siding; 'no exposure any side') (no street junction or other feature shared with the modern data; needs position of the brickworks (the key map puts it west of Zion Road near the Pleasantville line) from an old aerial or topographic map, as hand-picked control; step 6b).

sheet-4.description: The centre of Northfield between Fuae Avenue and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line, electric and steam) at the top and Shore Road, with the grounds of the Country Club of Atlantic City filling the lower half of the sheet. Davis, Mount Vernon, Ireland, Jackson, Fairbanks and Fair Way Avenues and Putting Green run down from the railroad, crossed by Broad and ending at Shore Road; Zion Road comes in diagonally at the left to meet Shore Road, and Hemsley Place leads down the left edge past the club grounds. Northfield station stands beside the track at the head of Ireland Avenue. The blocks between Broad and Shore Road are laid out in narrow lots with scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings, a few brick and concrete-block buildings, auto houses and stores; the Faith Tabernacle (hot air furnace, electric light) stands on Mount Vernon Avenue near Broad, and a large block east of Jackson Avenue is still undivided except for its frontage lots. South of Shore Road a few stores and dwellings face the road, and a 4-inch water pipe runs from Shore Road across the golf course to the frame club house with its hose cart and hydrants. A row of dwellings along Hemsley Place backs onto ground marked vacant beyond. 6- and 8-inch water pipes run along Fairbanks Avenue, Putting Green and Shore Road. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; sheet 2 adjoins above, sheet 5 on the left and sheet 3 on the right.
notes: Ireland Avenue is now the south end of Roosevelt Avenue; Fair Way is Fairway Avenue; Hemsley Place is now Helmsley Place.
Davis Avenue north of Broad is marked not opened.
Fairbanks Avenue and Fair Way are offset at Broad, so their junction with Broad Street was left out of the control.
Northfield station of the Shore Fast Line and the Faith Tabernacle; club house of the Country Club of Atlantic City.
Shore Road / Zion Road and Shore Road / Helmsley Place carry residuals of about 3 m.

100 ft. Fuae Av / railroad to Shore Rd: Davis, Mt. Vernon, Ireland (now Roosevelt Avenue), Jackson, Fairbanks, Fair Way (Fairway Avenue), Putting Green; Broad; Zion Rd, Hemsley Pl (now Helmsley Place). Northfield station, Faith Tabernacle, Country Club of Atlantic City club house.

sheet-5.description: The middle of Northfield around the Zion Road crossing of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line, electric and steam), which runs across the sheet with the Zion Road station. North of the track Zion Road and Tilton Road cross diagonally in the upper left, Northfield Avenue runs down from Tilton Road to Zion Road, a proposed street is drawn parallel to it, and at the right edge Davis Avenue meets First Avenue and Fuae Avenue; most of this ground is divided into long narrow lots with few buildings, among them the chapel of the Northfield M.E. Church. South of the track Wabash Avenue runs along the railroad, Northfield and Fifield Avenues run down to Shore Road with close-set frame dwellings, hen houses and the post office, Zion Road continues diagonally to the lower right, and Tilton Road and Northfield Plaza reach the left edge. Along Shore Road stand the City Hall with the fire department (concrete floor), cottages named The Maples, The Pines, The Nest and Yale Cottage, and the greenhouses of the Edwards Floral Hall Co. Hemsley Place leaves Shore Road at the lower right, Broad Street is marked not opened at the right edge, and the golf course of the Country Club of Atlantic City lies beyond the bottom of the sheet. An 8-inch water pipe runs along Shore Road and a 6-inch pipe along Northfield Avenue and Northfield Plaza. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; sheet 2 adjoins on the right above the railroad, sheet 4 on the right below it and sheet 6 on the left.
notes: Hemsley Place is now Helmsley Place; First Avenue is now 1st Street.

Modern Tilton Road and the north end of Northfield Avenue do not match the drawn junctions with Zion Road and Tilton Road (about 15 to 30 m off at the existing fit); they were not used, so the upper left of the sheet has no control.
Fifield Avenue / Wabash Avenue was rejected at 17 m: modern Wabash Avenue does not follow the 1924 street beside the track here.
City Hall and fire department, post office, chapel of the Northfield M.E. Church, Zion Road station, Edwards Floral Hall Co greenhouses.

100 ft. Zion Rd, Tilton Rd, Northfield Av, Fifield Av, Wabash Av, Shore Rd, Northfield Plaza, Hemsley Pl (now Helmsley Place), Davis Av, 1st Av (now 1st Street), Fuae Av, Broad St (not opened); Zion Road station, city hall and fire dept, post office, Northfield M.E. chapel, Edwards Floral Hall Co greenhouses. Modern Tilton Rd and north Northfield Av do not match the drawn junctions in the upper left (15-30 m); that area has no control.

sheet-6-1.description: The western side of central Northfield between the Zion Road area and Shore Road, crossed from side to side by the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line, electric and steam) with the Bakersville station and a freight depot where Mill Road crosses the track. North of the railroad Mill Road runs up the sheet past long strip lots with a few dwellings, a hot house and an office, Cedar Bridge Road comes in diagonally from the upper left, and a curving railroad siding leaves the main line to end at a building marked vacant; Zion Road crosses the upper right corner. South of the railroad Bargaintown Road and Cedar Bridge Road run diagonally down to Mill Road and Shore Road, with Keaton Place a short arbitrary lane off Mill Road, and Tilton Road leaves Shore Road at the foot of Mill Road for the upper right, passing the oval of Northfield Plaza. Most of the ground is in large tracts with scattered frame dwellings, stores, hen houses and stables, densest along Mill Road and Tilton Road near Shore Road. Along the bottom Shore Road carries an 8-inch water pipe, with Rosedale Avenue leaving it at the lower left and a lane at the lower right. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; a dash-dot match line A-B near the top marks where the inset in the upper left corner joins, sheet 5 adjoins on the right, sheet 7 on the left and sheet 8 below.
notes: Mill Road is now West Mill Road north of Shore Road (East Mill Road continues south); Shore Road, Mill Road and Tilton Road meet at one modern node.
Bargaintown Road south of the railroad no longer follows its 1924 line to Shore Road and was not used as control.
Bakersville station and freight depot of the Shore Fast Line at Mill Road; the railroad and its siding have since been removed.

Only five control points, three of them on Shore Road; Cedar Bridge Road / Mill Road and Northfield Plaza / Tilton Road were hand-picked and disagree by about 4 m in opposite directions. The upper half of the part has no control.

100 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main): Shore Rd, Mill Rd (now West Mill Road), Cedar Bridge Rd, Bargaintown Rd, Tilton Rd, Keaton Pl, Northfield Plaza, Rosedale Av; railroad with Bakersville station and a curving siding. Few junctions: 3 detected on Shore Rd plus 2 hand-picked. Part 2: inset at upper left behind a heavy line, continuing the sheet beyond its top edge (match line A-B): Zion Rd, Mill Rd, New Rd, Northfield Public School; two-point helmert.

sheet-6-2.description: A boxed inset in the upper left corner of sheet 6 that continues the sheet beyond its top edge, joined to the main map along the dash-dot match line A-B. It shows the junction of Zion Road and Mill Road in the far west of Northfield, with New Road leaving Zion Road to the east. Mill Road, carrying a 10-inch water pipe, runs down the inset; Zion Road, with a 12-inch water pipe, crosses it diagonally. The ground is in large tracts with a few one- and two-storey frame dwellings, stores and outbuildings along Mill Road and Zion Road, and the Northfield Public School (brick, steam heat, electric light) stands on a large lot on the west side of Mill Road. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch, at the same orientation as the main sheet.
notes: Mill Road is now West Mill Road.
Northfield Public School on Mill Road.

Placed by two junctions only (Zion Road with West Mill Road and with New Road), as a helmert transformation; the fitted scale is about 4 percent larger than the atlas scale, so expect a few metres of error away from these two points.

100 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main): Shore Rd, Mill Rd (now West Mill Road), Cedar Bridge Rd, Bargaintown Rd, Tilton Rd, Keaton Pl, Northfield Plaza, Rosedale Av; railroad with Bakersville station and a curving siding. Few junctions: 3 detected on Shore Rd plus 2 hand-picked. Part 2: inset at upper left behind a heavy line, continuing the sheet beyond its top edge (match line A-B): Zion Rd, Mill Rd, New Rd, Northfield Public School; two-point helmert.

sheet-7.description: The southwest end of Northfield against the Linwood boundary, drawn turned on the page so that the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Shore Fast Line, electric and steam) runs straight up the sheet and Shore Road lies along the right edge. Bargaintown Road crosses the upper left diagonally from Cedar Bridge Road, and Ridgewood Avenue, marked not opened, crosses the whole sheet; the upper half is otherwise long strips of open land with a few dwellings, poultry houses and a garage along Shore Road. In the lower half a newly platted grid of narrow lots runs along Revere, Oakcrest and Vernon Avenues, crossed by Fenton and Warren Avenues, with Wabash Avenue on both sides of the railroad and a second Revere Avenue running from Shore Road; dwellings are still few and scattered. A dash-dot line near the bottom marks the city line, below which the map of Linwood continues. Shore Road, about 50 to 70 feet wide, carries an 8-inch water pipe, and the streets of sheet 8 (Rosedale, Cove, Revere, Oakcrest and Vernon Avenues) are lettered as stubs on its far side. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; sheet 6 adjoins at the top and sheet 8 on the right.
notes: The sheet is turned on the page: north points to the upper left, about 90 degrees from the other sheets.
Revere, Oakcrest and Vernon Avenues are now West Revere, West Oakcrest and West Vernon Avenues; Ridgewood Avenue (not opened) does not match today's Ridgewood Drive and was not used.
Revere Avenue jogs at the railroad; modern Wabash Avenue has a node on each side of it, and both were accepted.
Warren Avenue / Vernon Avenue was detected about 28 ft off the drawn junction and excluded.
Control is loose: residuals of 2 to 10 m (RMSE 5.3 m); two points on Shore Road (Rosedale and Cove Avenues, drawn as stubs on the far side) were hand-picked.

100 ft, turned on the page (north to the upper left). Southwest end at the Linwood line: Bargaintown Rd, Ridgewood Av (not opened; not today's Ridgewood Drive), Revere, Oakcrest, Vernon (now West ...), Warren, Fenton, Wabash Avs on both sides of the railroad, Shore Rd along the right edge. Loose fit (RMSE about 5 m).

sheet-8.description: The south side of Shore Road at the southwest end of Northfield, running down towards the bay along the boundary with the Borough of Linwood, which is drawn as a dash-dot line at the left. Vernon, Oakcrest and Revere Avenues run down the sheet from Shore Road and are crossed by Franklin Avenue; the blocks are cut into narrow house lots with scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings, a few brick ones, and poultry houses, thinning out away from Shore Road. At the bottom the platted lots give way to a waterfront subdivision cut by four canals, lettered A to D, joined by a cross canal and drawn in blue, with rows of narrow lots between them. East of Revere Avenue a single large undivided tract runs from Shore Road to the bay with a few dwellings and poultry houses near the road, and along the right edge Cove Avenue runs down from Shore Road beside Rosedale Avenue, which is marked not opened. Shore Road, about 70 feet wide with an 8-inch water pipe, runs across the top, with Oakcrest and Ridgewood Avenues lettered on its far side. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; sheet 7 adjoins above and sheet 6 to the upper right.
notes: Vernon, Oakcrest and Revere Avenues are now East Vernon, East Oakcrest and East Revere Avenues; Franklin Avenue is now Swilkey Avenue.
Rosedale Avenue south of Shore Road is marked not opened.
The canal subdivision at the bottom of the sheet is drawn as platted lots between canals A to D, with no buildings.
100 ft. Shore Rd south side to the Linwood boundary: Vernon, Oakcrest, Revere (now East ...), Franklin Av (now Swilkey Avenue), Cove Av, Rosedale Av (not opened); canals A to D at the bottom.
